subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Shell Structures: Eggshell Engineering
description: One-minute skill: Shell Structures: Eggshell Engineering.

hook.text: An eggshell is 0.3 mm thick but can support 3 kg of weight. Curvature makes thin things strong.

buildup.text: Shell structures distribute forces across their curved surface. Compression flows in all directions, not just one.

discovery.text: The Sydney Opera House uses precast concrete shells. Each shell is a section cut from a single sphere.

twist.text: Thin shells are elegant but risky. A small imperfection can cause sudden catastrophic buckling.

climax.text: Modern stadiums use cable-reinforced shells spanning 200 meters with roofs just centimeters thick.

punchline.text: Thin, curved, and impossibly strong. Nature taught us that.

quiz.question: Why can thin shell structures carry such heavy loads?
options: The materials used in shells are denser than normal concrete
Curvature distributes forces across the entire surface in all directions
Shells trap air pressure inside that helps support the load
